descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Number Sense and Operations — Numbers to 20, Subitizing to 5, Composing/Decomposing to 10 (A6.1–A6.6)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Kindergarten unit on Number Sense and Operations (A6.1–A6.6), framed around Mae and Theo, two child chefs, and Buddy the puppy. Includes 5 lesson plans, 5 worksheets, 7 manipulatives, a full assessment suite, and a Junior Counting Crew certificate.
long_description:
Bring numbers to life in your Kindergarten classroom. The Counting Crew is a 5-day, ready-to-teach unit that takes children on a journey with Mae and Theo — two friendly child chefs — and Buddy the golden-retriever puppy to discover what numbers are for, how to count forward and backward, how to read and write the numerals 0–20, how to subitize small groups without counting, and finally how to build numbers in many different ways and compare groups using more, less, or equal.

Each lesson is fully scripted with teacher prompts, structured for play-based learning, and includes a printable student worksheet that consolidates the day's thinking. Children hunt for numbers around the room (Lesson 1), step forward and backward on a Counting Path floor mat (Lesson 2), match numerals to quantities and trace the tricky teens with the tens-stick model (Lesson 3), play subitizing flash games with Buddy's paw-print dot cards (Lesson 4), and finally compose 7 in three different ways and compare two plates of timbits as MORE, LESS, or EQUAL (Lesson 5).

What makes this unit different:
- Aligned to all six Ontario Kindergarten Number Sense and Operations expectations (A6.1–A6.6) — no gaps, no drift.
- A single coherent narrative across 5 days: recurring characters, threaded vocabulary, an anchor chart that grows day by day.
- Four-track differentiation built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners.
- Detailed teacher script for the conceptually trickiest moment — Lesson 3's tricky teens — including the 'thirty vs thirteen' confusion, expected student responses, and tens-stick recovery moves.
- Manipulatives ready to print (default black and white so any classroom printer works), plus reusable assessment trackers per lesson.
- Mid-unit formative check between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 to flag teen-recognition issues before subitizing builds on top.
- Student-friendly Junior Counting Crew certificate for the closing ceremony.

Designed for Canadian classrooms: Canadian counting objects (toonies, loonies, maple-leaf cards), Tim Hortons-style timbits in the comparison activity, the spelling 'colour' throughout, and Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions for assessment.

Total classroom time: about 205 minutes across 5 lessons. Teacher prep time: about 95 minutes one-time, then the printables are reusable next year. Suitable for Junior or Senior Kindergarten teachers in Ontario, or any teacher introducing the numerals 0–20, subitizing, composing/decomposing, and comparison language to 4–6 year olds.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans (40–45 minutes each, ~205 minutes total of teaching time)
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson, with name/date fields and child-voice learning goals
1 mid-unit formative assessment ('Numerals 0–20 Check-In') administered between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 prompts for student self-assessment

10 printable teacher manipulatives: counting cube storage mat, ten-frame mats, Buddy's paw-print subitizing dot cards, number cards 0–20, real-world counting objects sorting tray, more/less/equal comparison strip, Counting Path floor mat, plus Mae, Theo, and Buddy character puppets
4 class observation trackers: 1 diagnostic (Lesson 1) plus 3 formative (Lessons 2, 3, 4)
1 six-level summative rubric covering all six expectations (A6.1–A6.6)
1 summative administration guide tying the Lesson 5 worksheet, the lesson, and the rubric together for the teacher
Junior Counting Crew certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony, featuring Mae, Theo, and Buddy

Detailed expanded walkthrough for the keystone lesson (Lesson 3 — Number Letters), including the tens-stick recovery for the 'thirteen vs thirty' confusion, expected student responses, and recovery moves
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Junior or Senior Kindergarten teachers in Ontario, or any teacher introducing the numerals 0–20, subitizing, composing/decomposing, and comparison language (more / less / equal) to 4–6 year olds. Especially valuable for teachers who want a coherent multi-day unit rather than disconnected counting worksheets, and who want a tens-stick-based recovery for the tricky teens built into the lesson.
subject: Mathematics
strand: A. Foundations of Language and Mathematics — Number Sense and Operations
pedagogical_approach: Play-based, oral-first, movement-rich. Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression: linking cubes (concrete) → dot cards and number cards (representational) → written numerals plus comparison language (abstract). Worksheets are end-of-lesson consolidation, never the main activity. Student-generated counts and groupings are honoured. Assessment is observational and uses the Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions: descriptive, growth-oriented, and aligned to a 4-level rubric across each expectation.
